questions.question: What must be included in emergency response information?
questions.explanation: Emergency response information for hazardous materials must include details about fire or explosion risks.

questions.question: How do you show the difference between hazardous and non-hazardous materials on a shipping paper?

options.text: List the hazardous materials at the bottom of the paper.
List the hazardous materials at the top of the paper.
Highlight the hazardous materials in the same color as the non-hazardous materials.
Mark the non-hazardous materials with an "X."

questions.correctAnswerText: List the hazardous materials at the top of the paper.
questions.explanation: When a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, you must separate them in one of three ways: list hazardous materials first, highlight them in a different color, or mark them with an "X" in a column labeled "HM."

questions.question: When can a vehicle without proper placards be moved?

options.text: To make room for other vehicles.
If the vehicle will travel less than 10 miles.

questions.explanation: A vehicle must have proper placards before it is driven. An improperly placarded vehicle may only be moved if it is necessary to protect people or property in an emergency.

questions.question: What is the correct way to check tire pressure?

options.text: Push on the tire with your hand.
Measure the height of the tire.

questions.explanation: You must check your tires at the start of every trip and after every stop. The only way to check tire pressure correctly is to use a tire pressure gauge.

questions.question: What does a driver need to accept a hazardous materials package if it appears safe?
questions.explanation: Unless a package is clearly unsafe or breaks hazmat rules, you may accept the shipper's certification that it was packaged correctly.

questions.question: Which agency performs the background check for a HazMat endorsement?
questions.explanation: When you apply for a new or renewed HazMat endorsement, the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) must do a federal security background check.

questions.question: How can hazardous materials be marked on a shipping paper that lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials?

options.text: Highlight them in a contrasting color.
Circle them with a pen or marker.

questions.correctAnswerText: Highlight them in a contrasting color.
questions.explanation: When a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, hazardous materials must be separated in one of three ways: listed first, highlighted in a different color, or marked with an "X" in a column titled "HM."

questions.question: What should a driver verify before transporting materials?

options.text: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages.
The shipping paper is written in code.
All packages are labeled as poison.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages.
questions.explanation: Compare the package markings and labels to the shipping papers. Make sure the shipper wrote the correct description on the shipping paper and placed the correct labels on the packages.

questions.question: Who is responsible for marking and labeling hazardous materials for shipping?
questions.explanation: The shipper must correctly mark and label hazardous materials. The driver should check that the shipper did this before starting the trip.

questions.question: How should a trailer be cleaned after a corrosive material leaks inside?

options.text: Leave it to air-dry without washing.

questions.explanation: Any part of a vehicle exposed to a corrosive material must be thoroughly washed with water.

questions.question: What should a driver do if given a leaking package or shipment?

options.text: Leave it on the side of the road.

questions.explanation: Drivers must refuse any package or shipment of hazardous materials that leaks.

questions.question: Flammable gases are categorized as ____ hazards.
questions.explanation: Flammable gases are Class 2 hazardous materials.

questions.question: Which level of government controls hazardous materials laws?
questions.explanation: The federal, state, and local governments all set regulations for transporting hazardous materials because of the risks involved.

questions.question: Which agency conducts the security check for a HazMat endorsement?
questions.explanation: The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) conducts the security check needed to get a hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.question: What information does a shipping paper provide?

options.text: How the materials will be transported
Who should accept the materials being transported

questions.explanation: Shipping papers must describe the specific hazardous materials being transported.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, where should you NOT park your vehicle?
questions.explanation: Never park a vehicle carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building. Park at least 5 feet away from the road.

questions.question: What should you NOT use when loading hazardous materials containers?
questions.explanation: Never use hooks or other equipment that could damage containers when loading hazardous materials.

questions.question: What class hazard is an explosive material most likely to be?
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials are items that can explode or cause fires.

questions.question: Where should shipping papers be placed if you leave your vehicle while transporting hazardous materials?

options.text: Left in the front seat of the cab.
Placed in a box under the passenger seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left in the front seat of the cab.
questions.explanation: Leave shipping papers on the driver's seat when you exit your vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do with the engine when refueling a vehicle carrying hazardous materials?

options.text: Have someone other than the driver do it.

questions.explanation: Always turn off the engine before refueling. Someone must always be present at the nozzle.

questions.question: When loading compressed gas, should the liquid discharge valves be open or closed?
questions.explanation: During loading and unloading of compressed gas tanks, keep liquid discharge valves open. Close them at all other times.

questions.question: When transporting hazardous materials, where should placards be placed?

options.text: On all four sides of the vehicle
Only by Class A licensed drivers

questions.correctAnswerText: On all four sides of the vehicle
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be placed on all four sides of the vehicle when required.

questions.question: If the letter "G" appears in Column 1 of a shipping paper, what else must be shown?

options.text: The technical name of the hazardous material
The type of packaging containing the hazardous material
The date the product was packed

questions.correctAnswerText: The technical name of the hazardous material
questions.explanation: When "G" (for "Generic") appears in Column 1 of a shipping paper, you must also list the technical name of the hazardous material.

questions.question: What letters appear on shipping papers and packages for reportable quantities?
questions.explanation: The letters "RQ" must be displayed on shipping papers and packages when transporting a reportable quantity of hazardous materials.

questions.question: Hazardous materials regulations protect all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials regulations protect drivers, other people nearby, and the environment. Buildings are not specifically the target of these protections.

questions.question: What must a package display if it contains liquid containers?

options.text: Arrows pointing in the correct upright direction
The number of containers inside the box

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrows pointing in the correct upright direction
questions.explanation: Packages with liquid containers must display arrows showing which way is up. These orientation markers prevent the package from being turned sideways or upside down.

questions.question: What is important to know when transporting radioactive materials?

options.text: Radiation will pass through to other packages
The package should be placed in the cab
The package should be loaded on its side
The package should be made of wood

questions.correctAnswerText: Radiation will pass through to other packages
questions.explanation: Radiation passes through nearby packages. The number of radioactive packages that can be loaded together is limited to control radiation exposure.

questions.question: If corrosive materials leak in a trailer, how should it be cleaned?

options.text: Leave it to air dry without washing

questions.explanation: Parts exposed to corrosive liquids must be thoroughly washed with water.

questions.question: Who must provide emergency response information to drivers?
questions.explanation: Shippers of hazardous materials must provide emergency response information to drivers.

questions.question: When loading compressed gas, should liquid discharge valves be open or closed?
questions.explanation: During loading and unloading, keep liquid discharge valves on compressed gas tanks open. Keep them closed at all other times.
